Arrow–Debreu Equilibrium

An Edgeworth box in state-contingent consumption space. With no aggregate risk, both consumers sit on the 45-degree line in equilibrium — full insurance (mutuality principle). Move the aggregate-risk slider and everyone tracks the aggregate.

Examples & Exercises

With log utility, π1=1/2\pi_1 = 1/2π1​=1/2, aggregate endowments E1=E2=10E_1 = E_2 = 10E1​=E2​=10 (no aggregate risk), and e1=(7,3)e^1 = (7, 3)e1=(7,3), verify by direct computation that the Arrow–Debreu equilibrium gives both consumers full insurance (state-independent consumption).

qs=πs(W1+W2)Es,cis=πsWiqsq_s = \frac{\pi_s (W_1 + W_2)}{E_s}, \qquad c_{is} = \frac{\pi_s W_i}{q_s}qs​=Es​πs​(W1​+W2​)​,cis​=qs​πs​Wi​​
Show proof
  1. q1=0.5⋅20/10=1q_1 = 0.5 \cdot 20/10 = 1q1​=0.5⋅20/10=1, q2=1q_2 = 1q2​=1. Wealths: W1=7+3=10W_1 = 7 + 3 = 10W1​=7+3=10, W2=10W_2 = 10W2​=10.
  2. Demands are ci1=0.5⋅10/1=5c_{i1} = 0.5 \cdot 10/1 = 5ci1​=0.5⋅10/1=5, ci2=5c_{i2} = 5ci2​=5 — both consume state-independent (5,5)(5, 5)(5,5). This is the mutuality principle: with no aggregate risk, risk-averse consumers fully share idiosyncratic risk.

Introduce aggregate risk into the same setup: E1=12E_1 = 12E1​=12, E2=8E_2 = 8E2​=8. Find equilibrium consumption and show that aggregate risk cannot be insured away.

c11c12=E1E2=1.5\frac{c_{11}}{c_{12}} = \frac{E_1}{E_2} = 1.5c12​c11​​=E2​E1​​=1.5
Show proof
  1. q1:q2=0.512:0.58=2:3q_1 : q_2 = \frac{0.5}{12} : \frac{0.5}{8} = 2:3q1​:q2​=120.5​:80.5​=2:3. With r=q1/q2=2/3r = q_1/q_2 = 2/3r=q1​/q2​=2/3, W1=23⋅7+3=233W_1 = \frac{2}{3} \cdot 7 + 3 = \frac{23}{3}W1​=32​⋅7+3=323​.
  2. c11=0.5⋅233/23=5.75c_{11} = 0.5 \cdot \frac{23}{3} / \frac{2}{3} = 5.75c11​=0.5⋅323​/32​=5.75, c12=0.5⋅233=3.833c_{12} = 0.5 \cdot \frac{23}{3} = 3.833c12​=0.5⋅323​=3.833. And c11/c12=1.5=E1/E2c_{11}/c_{12} = 1.5 = E_1/E_2c11​/c12​=1.5=E1​/E2​: everyone's consumption moves in lockstep with the aggregate — aggregate risk can be shared but not eliminated.
